title: No, mother! Let me be and let me live.
html_source:
A possible allusion to the final scene in Hamlet as Hamlet dies. There, the ghost of his father is put to rest; here, Stephen sends the ghost of his mother away.

In Hamlet, “But let it be” is the culmination of the motif which commenced in the “To be or not to be” speech and was picked up again just before the duel, when he finally “let be” in the “special providence in the fall of a sparrow” speech.

HAMLET
Heaven make thee free of it! I follow thee.
I am dead, Horatio. Wretched queen, adieu!
You that look pale and tremble at this chance,
That are but mutes or audience to this act,
Had I but time—as this fell sergeant, death,
Is strict in his arrest—O, I could tell you—
But let it be. Horatio, I am dead;
Thou livest. Report me and my cause aright
To the unsatisfied.
